# Setup 

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)
library(patchwork)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(corrplot)
library(ggh4x)
library(segmented)
library(pROC)

combine_files <- function(folder_path, pattern) {
  matching_files <- list.files(
    path = folder_path,
    pattern = pattern,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  
  combined_data <- matching_files %>%
    map_dfr(~ read_csv(.x, col_types = cols(huc4 = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE))
  
  return(combined_data)
}

## Point Data

```{r}
s2_indices<- combine_files(folder_path = paste0(dat_path,'dataIn/RS_Data/'),pattern='s2_idx_alt_points') %>% 
    dplyr::rename_with(
    ~ .x %>%
        stringr::str_replace("_ndwi_ns$", "_ndmi") %>%
        stringr::str_replace("_ndwi_gs$", "_mndwi")
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(EvaluationID=EvltnID, year, ma_ndvi:so_vsdi) %>% 
  pivot_longer(ma_ndvi:so_vsdi, values_to = 'rs_value') %>% 
  mutate(
    footprint = 'plot center',
    spatial_reducer = 'point',
    satellite ='S2',
    temporal_reducer = 'mean'
  ) %>% 
  separate(name, into=c('season','rs_index')) %>% 
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels=c('ma','mj','ja','so'), labels=c("Mar-Apr",'May-Jun','Jul-Aug','Sep-Oct')))

s2_poly_indices<- combine_files(folder_path = paste0(dat_path,'dataIn/RS_Data/'),pattern='s2_idx_alt_thr_polygons') %>% 
    dplyr::rename_with(
    ~ .x %>%
        stringr::str_replace("_ndwi_ns$", "_ndmi") %>%
        stringr::str_replace("_ndwi_gs$", "_mndwi")
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(EvaluationID=Evaluation, year, ma_ndvi:so_vsdi) %>% 
  pivot_longer(ma_ndvi:so_vsdi, values_to = 'rs_value') %>% 
  mutate(
    footprint = 'plot polygon',
    spatial_reducer = 'median',
    satellite ='S2',
    temporal_reducer = 'mean'
  ) %>% 
  separate(name, into=c('season','rs_index')) %>% 
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels=c('ma','mj','ja','so'), labels=c("Mar-Apr",'May-Jun','Jul-Aug','Sep-Oct')))

s2_poly_pctarea<- combine_files(folder_path = paste0(dat_path,'dataIn/RS_Data/'),pattern='s2_idx_alt_thr_polygons') %>% 
  dplyr::select(EvaluationID=Evaluation, year, ma_ndvi_gt_0_1:so_ndvi_gt_0_4) %>% 
  pivot_longer(ma_ndvi_gt_0_1:so_ndvi_gt_0_4, values_to = 'rs_value') %>% 
  mutate(
    footprint = 'plot polygon',
    spatial_reducer = 'pctarea',
    satellite ='S2',
    temporal_reducer = 'mean'
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    t = case_when(
      str_detect(name, '0_1') ~ '0.1',
      str_detect(name, '0_2') ~ '0.2',
      str_detect(name, '0_3') ~ '0.3',
      str_detect(name, '0_4') ~ '0.4'
    ),
    spatial_reducer= paste0(spatial_reducer, '-',t)
  ) %>% 
  separate(name, into=c('season','rs_index',NA,NA)) %>% 
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels=c('ma','mj','ja','so'), labels=c("Mar-Apr",'May-Jun','Jul-Aug','Sep-Oct'))) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-t)

mrrmaid_indices<- combine_files(folder_path = paste0(dat_path,'dataIn/RS_Data/'),pattern='mrrmaid') %>% 
  dplyr::select(EvaluationID=Evaluation, year, month, prop_class_1:prop_class_5) %>% 
  pivot_longer(prop_class_1:prop_class_5, values_to = 'rs_value') %>% 
  mutate(
    footprint = 'plot polygon',
    spatial_reducer = 'pctarea',
    satellite ='S2',
    temporal_reducer = 'monthly'
  ) %>% 
  separate(name, into=c(NA,NA,'class_val')) %>% 
  mutate(
    class_name = 
      case_when(
       class_val =='1' ~ 'Upland',
       class_val =='2' ~ 'Mesic',
       class_val =='3' ~'Water',
       class_val =='4' ~ 'Snow',
       class_val == '5' ~ 'Shadow'
      ),
    month_abbr = case_when(
      month == 6 ~ 'Jun',
      month == 7 ~ 'Jul',
      month == 8 ~ 'Aug',
      month == 9 ~ 'Sep'
    ),
    rs_metric =  paste0('mrrmaid-',class_name,'-',month_abbr)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-class_name,-class_val,-month, -month_abbr)

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
# Calculate summary statistics for each group
summary_stats <- sites_w_meta %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  summarise(
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Function to calculate density at specific points
get_density_at_point <- function(data, point) {
  d <- density(data, na.rm = TRUE)
  approx(d$x, d$y, xout = point)$y
}

# Calculate density heights at quartile positions
summary_stats_with_density <- sites_w_meta %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  do({
    current_data <- .$value
    data.frame(
      name = unique(.$name),
      median = median(current_data, na.rm = TRUE),
      q1 = quantile(current_data, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q3 = quantile(current_data, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_density = get_density_at_point(current_data, median(current_data, na.rm = TRUE)),
      q1_density = get_density_at_point(current_data, quantile(current_data, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
      q3_density = get_density_at_point(current_data, quantile(current_data, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
  })

# Print the summary statistics
print("Summary Statistics:")
print(summary_stats_with_density)

# Calculate bounded densities for each group
density_data <- sites_w_meta %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  do({
    vals <- .$value[!is.na(.$value)]
    d <- density(vals, from = min(vals), to = max(vals))
    data.frame(
      name = unique(.$name),
      x = d$x,
      y = d$y
    )
  })

# Create the plot using geom_ribbon with bounded densities
p <- ggplot() +
  # Grey background density
  geom_density(data = all_sites_w_meta, aes(x = value), 
               alpha = 0.3, fill = 'grey50') +
  # Main density with bounded calculation
  geom_ribbon(data = density_data, aes(x = x, ymin = 0, ymax = y),
              fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.8,color='black') +
  # Median line
  geom_segment(data = summary_stats_with_density, 
               aes(x = median, xend = median, y = 0, yend = median_density), 
               color = "red", linetype = "solid", size = 1) +
  # Q1 line
  geom_segment(data = summary_stats_with_density, 
               aes(x = q1, xend = q1, y = 0, yend = q1_density), 
               color = "orange", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
  # Q3 line
  geom_segment(data = summary_stats_with_density, 
               aes(x = q3, xend = q3, y = 0, yend = q3_density), 
               color = "orange", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = 'free') +
  labs(
    title = "Density Plots with Median and Quartiles",
    subtitle = "Blue density curve is data at study area sites only\nRed line = Median, Orange dashed lines = Q1 and Q3\nGrey density curve is all 2022-2024 AIM RW sites",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Display the plot

# AIM Field Indicator Exploratory Analysis

```{r density plots}
# Field Indicator Distributions
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)


# Function to create density plots with quartile lines
plot_density_with_quartiles <- function(data, 
                                        data_all,
                                       value_col = "value", 
                                       group_col = "name",
                                       title = "Density Plots with Median and Quartiles",
                                       subtitle = "Blue density curve is data at study area sites only\nRed line = Median, Orange dashed lines = Q1 and Q3\nGrey density curve is all 2022-2024 AIM RW sites only",
                                       x_label = "Value",
                                       y_label = "Density",
                                       fill_color = "lightblue",
                                       fill_alpha = 0.7,
                                       median_color = "red",
                                       quartile_color = "orange",
                                       print_stats = TRUE) {
  
  # Helper function to calculate density at specific points
  get_density_at_point <- function(data, point) {
    d <- density(data, na.rm = TRUE)
    approx(d$x, d$y, xout = point)$y
  }
  
  # Use NSE (non-standard evaluation) to handle column names
  value_sym <- rlang::sym(value_col)
  group_sym <- rlang::sym(group_col)
  
  # Calculate density heights at quartile positions
  summary_stats_with_density <- data %>%
    group_by(!!group_sym) %>%
    summarise(
      median = median(!!value_sym, na.rm = TRUE),
      q1 = quantile(!!value_sym, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q3 = quantile(!!value_sym, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_density = get_density_at_point(!!value_sym, median(!!value_sym, na.rm = TRUE)),
      q1_density = get_density_at_point(!!value_sym, quantile(!!value_sym, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
      q3_density = get_density_at_point(!!value_sym, quantile(!!value_sym, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  # Print summary statistics if requested
  if (print_stats) {
    cat("Summary Statistics:\n")
    print(summary_stats_with_density)
  }
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- data %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = !!value_sym)) +
    geom_density(data=data_all,aes( x= !!value_sym), alpha=0.3,fill='grey50')+
    geom_density(fill = fill_color, alpha = fill_alpha) +
    # Median line
    geom_segment(data = summary_stats_with_density, 
                 aes(x = median, xend = median, y = 0, yend = median_density), 
                 color = median_color, linetype = "solid", size = 1) +
    # Q1 line
    geom_segment(data = summary_stats_with_density, 
                 aes(x = q1, xend = q1, y = 0, yend = q1_density), 
                 color = quartile_color, linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
    # Q3 line
    geom_segment(data = summary_stats_with_density, 
                 aes(x = q3, xend = q3, y = 0, yend = q3_density), 
                 color = quartile_color, linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", group_col)), scales = 'free') +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # Return both the plot and the statistics
  return(list(plot = p, stats = summary_stats_with_density))
}

plot_cdf <- function(data_full, data_subset, column, x_label = NULL, reverse_x = FALSE) {
  
  # Arrange and calculate cumulative counts
  if (reverse_x) {
    data_sorted <- data_full %>%
      arrange(desc({{ column }})) %>%
      mutate(cumulative_count = row_number())
    
    data_sorted_subset <- data_subset %>%
      arrange(desc({{ column }})) %>%
      mutate(cumulative_count = row_number())
  } else {
    data_sorted <- data_full %>%
      arrange({{ column }}) %>%
      mutate(cumulative_count = row_number())
    
    data_sorted_subset <- data_subset %>%
      arrange({{ column }}) %>%
      mutate(cumulative_count = row_number())
  }
  
  total_n <- nrow(data_sorted)
  
  # Default x-axis label if not provided
  if (is.null(x_label)) {
    x_label <- deparse(substitute(column))
  }
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(data_sorted, aes(x = {{ column }}, y = cumulative_count)) +
    geom_step() +
    geom_step(data = data_sorted_subset, color = 'red') +
    labs(
      x = x_label,
      y = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_few() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, NA),
      breaks = c(0, 50, 100, 250, 500, 750, 1000, 1250),
      expand = c(0, 0),  # Remove padding on y-axis
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / total_n * 100, 
                          name = "Percent Total")
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits=c(0,100))  # Remove padding on x-axis
  
  # Add reversed x-axis if requested
  if (reverse_x) {
    p <- p + scale_x_reverse(expand = c(0, 0))
  }
  
  return(p)
}

#Function to find significant breakpoints using only Davies' test
find_significant_thresholds <- function(data,alpha=0.2) {
  results <- data.frame(
    field_indicator = character(),
    rs_metric = character(),
    threshold = numeric(),
    p_value = numeric(),
    significant = logical(),
    plateau_cor = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (fi in unique(data$field_indicators)) {
    for (rm in unique(data$rs_metric)) {
      subset_data <- data %>% 
        filter(field_indicators == fi, rs_metric == rm) %>%
        arrange(width_midpoints)
      
      if (nrow(subset_data) < 6) next
      
      # Fit linear model first
      lm_fit <- lm(cor ~ width_midpoints, data = subset_data)
      
      # Run Davies' test with recommended k value (k=10)
      tryCatch({
        # Test if a breakpoint exists
        davies <- davies.test(lm_fit, ~width_midpoints, k = 10)
        p_value <- davies$p.value
        
        # Only proceed with segmented regression if Davies' test is significant
        if (p_value < alpha) {
          # Fit segmented model
          seg_fit <- segmented(lm_fit, seg.Z = ~width_midpoints, 
                              psi = median(subset_data$width_midpoints))
          
          # Extract threshold
          threshold <- seg_fit$psi[,"Est."]
          
          # Calculate plateau correlation
          plateau_data <- subset_data %>% filter(width_midpoints >= threshold)
          plateau_cor <- mean(plateau_data$cor, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          # Add to results
          results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
            field_indicator = fi,
            rs_metric = rm,
            threshold = threshold,
            p_value = p_value,
            significant = TRUE,  # Always TRUE since we're only adding if p_value < 0.05
            plateau_cor = plateau_cor,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
          ))
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        # Print error to help debugging
        cat("Error with", fi, rm, ":", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
      })
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# Function to plot only significant breakpoints
plot_significant_thresholds <- function(data, thresholds,alpha) {
  # Create a complete dataset that includes all combinations
  all_combos <- expand.grid(
    field_indicators = unique(data$field_indicators),
    rs_metric = unique(data$rs_metric),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Left join with the threshold results (only significant ones will have values)
  plot_data <- all_combos %>%
    left_join(thresholds, 
              by = c("field_indicators" = "field_indicator", 
                    "rs_metric" = "rs_metric")) %>%
    left_join(data, by = c("field_indicators", "rs_metric"))
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(width_midpoints, cor)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(span = 1, se = FALSE, color = "#4575B4", linewidth = 1) +
    
    # Only add threshold lines if significant (not NA)
    geom_vline(data = filter(plot_data, !is.na(threshold)),
               aes(xintercept = threshold), 
               color = "#D73027", linetype = "dashed") +
    
    geom_hline(data = filter(plot_data, !is.na(plateau_cor)),
               aes(yintercept = plateau_cor), 
               color = "#4DAF4A", linetype = "dashed") +
    
    # Add annotations only for significant breakpoints
    geom_text(data = filter(plot_data, !is.na(threshold)),
              aes(x = threshold, y = min(cor, na.rm = TRUE),
                  label = sprintf("Threshold: %.1f m", threshold, p_value)),
              color = "#D73027", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0, size = 2.5) +
    
    facet_grid(rows = vars(field_indicators), 
               cols = vars(rs_metric), 
               scales = 'free') +
    
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#5b7fa3"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "white"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = "Plot Width Thresholds for Field-RS Correlations",
      subtitle = paste0("Red lines indicate estimated breakpoint locations from segmented regression. Breakpoints shown only when \nDavies' test (p < ", alpha, ") provides evidence that a breakpoint exists. Green lines indicate mean correlations \nfor plot widths above the breakpoint." ),
      x = "Plot Width (m)",
      y = "Correlation (rho)"
    )
  
  return(p)
}

library(betareg)

#' Simple Beta Regression for Mapping Over Grouped Data
#' 
#' Fits beta regression with automatic link selection for a single dataset
#'
#' @param data Data frame with predictor and response columns
#' @return List with model stats, plot, and plot data

fit_beta_model <- function(data) {
  
  response <- data$field_indicators[1]
  predictor <- data$rs_metric[1]
  
  # Prepare data
  x <-  data$rs_value
  y <-  data$field_value / 100  # Transform to 0-1
  
  # Handle boundaries
  y[y == 0] <- 0.001
  y[y == 1] <- 0.999
  
  # Remove missing values
  complete_idx <- complete.cases(x, y)
  x <- x[complete_idx]
  y <- y[complete_idx]
  
  model_data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
  
  # Test link functions
  logit_model <- betareg(y ~ x, data = model_data, link = "logit")
  probit_model <- betareg(y ~ x, data = model_data, link = "probit")
  cloglog_model <- betareg(y ~ x, data = model_data, link = "cloglog")
  
  # Select best model by BIC
  bics <- c(logit = BIC(logit_model), 
            probit = BIC(probit_model), 
            cloglog = BIC(cloglog_model))
  
  best_link <- names(which.min(bics))
  best_model <- get(paste0(best_link, "_model"))
  
  # Create predictions for plot
  x_seq <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100)
  pred_data <- data.frame(x = x_seq)
  
  # Get model matrix for new predictions
  X_new <- model.matrix(~ x, data = pred_data)
  
   # Get coefficient covariance matrix (only for mean parameters)
  vcov_full <- vcov(best_model)
  n_mean_coefs <- ncol(X_new)
  vcov_mean <- vcov_full[1:n_mean_coefs, 1:n_mean_coefs]
  
  # Calculate standard errors on link scale
  # SE = sqrt(X * Vcov * X')
  pred_se_link <- sqrt(rowSums((X_new %*% vcov_mean) * X_new))
  
  # Get predictions on link scale
  pred_link <- predict(best_model, newdata = pred_data, type = "link")
  
  # Calculate confidence intervals on link scale
  lower_link <- pred_link - 1.96 * pred_se_link
  upper_link <- pred_link + 1.96 * pred_se_link
  
  # Transform to response scale using inverse link function
  if (best_link == "logit") {
    fitted <- plogis(pred_link)
    lower <- plogis(lower_link)
    upper <- plogis(upper_link)
  } else if (best_link == "probit") {
    fitted <- pnorm(pred_link)
    lower <- pnorm(lower_link)
    upper <- pnorm(upper_link)
  } else {  # cloglog
    fitted <- 1 - exp(-exp(pred_link))
    lower <- 1 - exp(-exp(lower_link))
    upper <- 1 - exp(-exp(upper_link))
  }
  
  # Extract precision parameter from model
  phi <- best_model$coefficients$precision
  
  # Compute 95% prediction interval bounds
  # qbeta() gives the quantiles of the Beta distribution
  lower_pred <- qbeta(0.025, shape1 = fitted * phi, shape2 = (1 - fitted) * phi)
  upper_pred <- qbeta(0.975, shape1 = fitted * phi, shape2 = (1 - fitted) * phi)
  
  # Create plot data table (convert back to 0-100 scale)
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    predictor_name = predictor,
    response_name = response,
    predictor_value = x_seq,
    fitted = fitted * 100,
    lower_ci = lower * 100,
    upper_ci = upper * 100,
    lower_pred = lower_pred * 100,
    upper_pred = upper_pred * 100
  )
  
  # Create observed data table
  obs_data <- data.frame(
    predictor_name = predictor,
    response_name = response,
    predictor_value = x, 
    observed_value = y * 100
  )
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = obs_data, aes(x = predictor_value, y = observed_value), alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(data = plot_data, aes(x = predictor_value, y = fitted), color = "red", size = 1) +
    geom_ribbon(data = plot_data, aes(x = predictor_value, ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci),
              fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +  # Confidence interval
    geom_ribbon(data = plot_data, aes(x = predictor_value, ymin = lower_pred, ymax = upper_pred),
              fill = "blue", alpha = 0.1) +  # Prediction interval
    labs(
      title = paste(predictor, "vs", response),
      subtitle = paste0("Link: ", best_link, ", Pseudo R² = ", round(best_model$pseudo.r.squared, 3)),
      x = predictor,
      y = response
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # Return results including plot data
  list(
    predictor = predictor,
    response = response,
    link = best_link,
    pseudo_r2 = best_model$pseudo.r.squared,
    aic = AIC(best_model),
    bic = BIC(best_model),
    p_value = summary(best_model)$coefficients$mean[2, 4],
    n = length(x),
    model = best_model,
    plot = p,
    plot_data = plot_data,        # NEW: Prediction data for plotting
    observed_data = obs_data      # NEW: Observed data for plotting
  )
}

safe_fit_beta_model <- safely(fit_beta_model)

# Example: How to create combined plots for the same response variable
# with different predictors on the same scale

create_combined_plot <- function(results_list, response_var, predictor1, predictor2) {
  
  # Extract relevant results
  result1 <- results_list %>% keep(~ .x$response == response_var & .x$predictor == predictor1) %>% .[[1]]
  result2 <- results_list %>% keep(~ .x$response == response_var & .x$predictor == predictor2) %>% .[[1]]
  
  if(is.null(result1) || is.null(result2)) {
    stop("One or both predictor-response combinations not found in results")
  }
  
  # Combine plot data with pseudo R² info
  combined_plot_data <- bind_rows(
    result1$plot_data %>% mutate(model = paste0("Model 1: ", predictor1, " (R² = ", round(result1$pseudo_r2, 3), ")")),
    result2$plot_data %>% mutate(model = paste0("Model 2: ", predictor2, " (R² = ", round(result2$pseudo_r2, 3), ")"))
  )
  
  # Combine observed data with pseudo R² info
  combined_obs_data <- bind_rows(
    result1$observed_data %>% mutate(model = paste0("Model 1: ", predictor1, " (R² = ", round(result1$pseudo_r2, 3), ")")),
    result2$observed_data %>% mutate(model = paste0("Model 2: ", predictor2, " (R² = ", round(result2$pseudo_r2, 3), ")"))
  )
  
  # Determine which model has better fit
  better_model <- ifelse(result1$pseudo_r2 > result2$pseudo_r2, predictor1, predictor2)
  better_r2 <- max(result1$pseudo_r2, result2$pseudo_r2)
  
  # Create combined plot
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = combined_obs_data, 
               aes(x = predictor_value, y = observed_value, color = model), 
               alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(data = combined_plot_data, 
              aes(x = predictor_value, y = fitted, color = model), 
              size = 1) +
    geom_ribbon(data = combined_plot_data, 
                aes(x = predictor_value, ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci, fill = model),
                alpha = 0.2) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Comparison of predictors for", response_var),
      subtitle = paste("Best model:", better_model, "with Pseudo R² =", round(better_r2, 3)),
      x = "Predictor Value",
      y = response_var,
      color = "Model",
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 9))+
    scale_color_few()+
    scale_fill_few(guide='none')
}

library(betareg)

#' Simple Beta Regression for Mapping Over Grouped Data
#' 
#' Fits beta regression with automatic link selection for a single dataset
#'
#' @param data Data frame with predictor and response columns
#' @return List with model stats, plot, and plot data
data <- dat_split[[1]]
fit_beta_model <- function(data) {
  
  response <- data$field_indicators[1]
  predictor <- data$rs_metric[1]
  wetland_type <-  data$WetlandType[1]
  # Prepare data
  x <-  data$rs_value
  y <-  data$field_value / 100  # Transform to 0-1
  
  # Handle boundaries
  y[y == 0] <- 0.001
  y[y == 1] <- 0.999
  
  # Remove missing values
  complete_idx <- complete.cases(x, y)
  x <- x[complete_idx]
  y <- y[complete_idx]
  
  model_data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
  
  # Test link functions
  logit_model <- betareg(y ~ x, data = model_data, link = "logit")
  probit_model <- betareg(y ~ x, data = model_data, link = "probit")
  cloglog_model <- betareg(y ~ x, data = model_data, link = "cloglog")
  
  # Select best model by BIC
  bics <- c(logit = BIC(logit_model), 
            probit = BIC(probit_model), 
            cloglog = BIC(cloglog_model))
  
  best_link <- names(which.min(bics))
  best_model <- get(paste0(best_link, "_model"))
  
  # Create predictions for plot
  x_seq <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100)
  pred_data <- data.frame(x = x_seq)
  
  # Get model matrix for new predictions
  X_new <- model.matrix(~ x, data = pred_data)
  
   # Get coefficient covariance matrix (only for mean parameters)
  vcov_full <- vcov(best_model)
  n_mean_coefs <- ncol(X_new)
  vcov_mean <- vcov_full[1:n_mean_coefs, 1:n_mean_coefs]
  
  # Calculate standard errors on link scale
  # SE = sqrt(X * Vcov * X')
  pred_se_link <- sqrt(rowSums((X_new %*% vcov_mean) * X_new))
  
  # Get predictions on link scale
  pred_link <- predict(best_model, newdata = pred_data, type = "link")
  
  # Calculate confidence intervals on link scale
  lower_link <- pred_link - 1.96 * pred_se_link
  upper_link <- pred_link + 1.96 * pred_se_link
  
  # Transform to response scale using inverse link function
  if (best_link == "logit") {
    fitted <- plogis(pred_link)
    lower <- plogis(lower_link)
    upper <- plogis(upper_link)
  } else if (best_link == "probit") {
    fitted <- pnorm(pred_link)
    lower <- pnorm(lower_link)
    upper <- pnorm(upper_link)
  } else {  # cloglog
    fitted <- 1 - exp(-exp(pred_link))
    lower <- 1 - exp(-exp(lower_link))
    upper <- 1 - exp(-exp(upper_link))
  }
  
  # Extract precision parameter from model
  phi <- best_model$coefficients$precision
  
  # Compute 95% prediction interval bounds
  # qbeta() gives the quantiles of the Beta distribution
  lower_pred <- qbeta(0.025, shape1 = fitted * phi, shape2 = (1 - fitted) * phi)
  upper_pred <- qbeta(0.975, shape1 = fitted * phi, shape2 = (1 - fitted) * phi)
  
  # Create plot data table (convert back to 0-100 scale)
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    predictor_name = predictor,
    response_name = response,
    wetlandtype = wetland_type,
    predictor_value = x_seq,
    fitted = fitted * 100,
    lower_ci = lower * 100,
    upper_ci = upper * 100,
    lower_pred = lower_pred * 100,
    upper_pred = upper_pred * 100
  )
  
  # Create observed data table
  obs_data <- data.frame(
    predictor_name = predictor,
    response_name = response,
    wetlandtype = wetland_type,
    predictor_value = x, 
    observed_value = y * 100
  )
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = obs_data, aes(x = predictor_value, y = observed_value), alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(data = plot_data, aes(x = predictor_value, y = fitted), color = "red", size = 1) +
    geom_ribbon(data = plot_data, aes(x = predictor_value, ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci),
              fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +  # Confidence interval
    geom_ribbon(data = plot_data, aes(x = predictor_value, ymin = lower_pred, ymax = upper_pred),
              fill = "blue", alpha = 0.1) +  # Prediction interval
    labs(
      title = paste(wetland_type, ': ',predictor, "vs", response),
      subtitle = paste0("Link: ", best_link, ", Pseudo R² = ", round(best_model$pseudo.r.squared, 3)),
      x = predictor,
      y = response
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # Return results including plot data
  list(
    predictor = predictor,
    response = response,
    link = best_link,
    wetland_type = wetland_type,
    pseudo_r2 = best_model$pseudo.r.squared,
    aic = AIC(best_model),
    bic = BIC(best_model),
    p_value = summary(best_model)$coefficients$mean[2, 4],
    n = length(x),
    model = best_model,
    plot = p,
    plot_data = plot_data,        # NEW: Prediction data for plotting
    observed_data = obs_data      # NEW: Observed data for plotting
  )
}

    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position= c(.9,.15),
  )+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(0,.25,.5,.75,1))

# Simplified NDVI Threshold Classification Analysis
# Tests NDVI thresholds to predict field indicator classifications


# Functionalized Threshold Analysis using Youden's J
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(pROC)

# Main analysis function
analyze_thresholds <- function(data, field_indicators, rs_indicators, field_thresholds = c(50, 75)) {
  
  # Helper function to find optimal threshold for one combination
  find_optimal <- function(data, field_col, rs_col, field_thresh) {
    field_binary <- ifelse(data[[field_col]] > field_thresh, 1, 0)
    roc_obj <- roc(field_binary, data[[rs_col]], quiet = TRUE)
    
    roc_data <- data.frame(
      sensitivity = roc_obj$sensitivities,
      specificity = roc_obj$specificities,
      threshold = roc_obj$thresholds
    )
    
    roc_data$youden_j <- roc_data$sensitivity + roc_data$specificity - 1
    optimal_idx <- which.max(roc_data$youden_j)
    
    return(data.frame(
      field_indicator = field_col,
      rs_indicator = rs_col,
      field_threshold = field_thresh,
      optimal_rs_threshold = roc_data$threshold[optimal_idx],
      sensitivity = roc_data$sensitivity[optimal_idx],
      specificity = roc_data$specificity[optimal_idx],
      youden_j = roc_data$youden_j[optimal_idx],
      auc = as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
    ))
  }
  
  # Generate all combinations and calculate optimal thresholds
  combinations <- expand.grid(
    field_indicator = field_indicators,
    rs_indicator = rs_indicators,
    field_threshold = field_thresholds,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  results <- pmap_dfr(combinations, function(field_indicator, rs_indicator, field_threshold) {
    find_optimal(data, field_indicator, rs_indicator, field_threshold)
  })
  
  return(results)
}

# Function to create classification and plots
create_classification_plots <- function(data, results) {
  
  plots_list <- list()
  
  for(i in 1:nrow(results)) {
    # Extract parameters for this combination
    field_col <- results$field_indicator[i]
    rs_col <- results$rs_indicator[i]
    field_thresh <- results$field_threshold[i]
    rs_thresh <- results$optimal_rs_threshold[i]
    
    # Classify points
    plot_data <- data %>%
      mutate(
        result = case_when(
          .data[[rs_col]] >= rs_thresh & .data[[field_col]] >= field_thresh ~ 'TP',
          .data[[rs_col]] < rs_thresh & .data[[field_col]] >= field_thresh ~ 'FN',
          .data[[rs_col]] < rs_thresh & .data[[field_col]] < field_thresh ~ 'TN',
          .data[[rs_col]] >= rs_thresh & .data[[field_col]] < field_thresh ~ 'FP'
        )
      )
    
    plot_title <- sprintf("%s vs %s (Field: >%d%%)", rs_col, field_col, field_thresh)
    
    # All data plot
    p_all <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = rs_col, y = field_col, color = "result")) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = field_thresh, linetype = "dashed") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = rs_thresh, linetype = "dashed") +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("TP" = "#2E8B57", "TN" = "#4169E1", 
                                   "FP" = "#FF6347", "FN" = "#FFD700")) +
      labs(title = paste("All Data:", plot_title),
           subtitle = sprintf("Overall Sens: %.3f, Spec: %.3f, Optimal Threshold: %.3f", 
                            results$sensitivity[i], results$specificity[i], results$optimal_rs_threshold[i])) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    
    # Faceted plot by WetlandType
    p_facet <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = rs_col, y = field_col, color = "result")) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = field_thresh, linetype = "dashed") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = rs_thresh, linetype = "dashed") +
      facet_wrap(~WetlandType) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("TP" = "#2E8B57", "TN" = "#4169E1", 
                                   "FP" = "#FF6347", "FN" = "#FFD700")) +
      labs(title = paste("By Wetland Type:", plot_title),
           subtitle = sprintf("Overall Sens: %.3f, Spec: %.3f, Optimal Threshold: %.3f", 
                            results$sensitivity[i], results$specificity[i], results$optimal_rs_threshold[i])) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    
    plots_list[[paste0("all_", i)]] <- p_all
    plots_list[[paste0("faceted_", i)]] <- p_facet
  }
  
  return(plots_list)
}

  filter(AvgWidthArea_1 > 10) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    EvaluationID, WetlandType, AH_HydroWithFACCover, AH_HydroNoFACCover, s2_jas_ndvi_median,s2_jas_ndvi_median_p90,
         S2_jas_ndvi_median_pctarea_gt0.4= `S2_jas_ndvi_median_pctarea-gt0.4`,

  mutate(WetlandType = ifelse(WetlandType == 'Riparian Shrubland', 'Riparian Shrubland or Shrub Wetland',WetlandType ))

# Define your indicators
field_indicators <- c("AH_HydroWithFACCover", "AH_HydroNoFACCover")

                   "S2_jas_MRRMAID_MesicmeanpctArea","S2_jasMVP_m0.2_mci0.3_mean_mean")

# Function to export plots with distinct names
export_plots <- function(plots_list, results, 
                        output_dir = "AIM_RW/figures/classification", 
                        file_format = "png", 
                        width = 10, 
                        height = 8, 
                        dpi = 300) {
  
  # Create output directory if it doesn't exist
  if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
    dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Helper function to clean names for filenames
  clean_name <- function(name) {
    # Replace special characters with underscores and remove extra spaces
    name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", name)
    name <- gsub("_{2,}", "_", name)  # Replace multiple underscores with single
    name <- gsub("^_|_$", "", name)   # Remove leading/trailing underscores
    return(name)
  }
  
  # Export each plot
  for(i in 1:nrow(results)) {
    
    # Get plot parameters
    field_indicator <- clean_name(results$field_indicator[i])
    rs_indicator <- clean_name(results$rs_indicator[i])
    field_threshold <- results$field_threshold[i]
    
    # Create base filename
    base_name <- sprintf("%s_vs_%s_thresh%d", 
                        rs_indicator, 
                        field_indicator, 
                        field_threshold)
    
    # Export "all data" plot
    all_plot_name <- paste0("all_", i)
    if (all_plot_name %in% names(plots_list)) {
      filename_all <- file.path(output_dir, 
                               paste0(base_name, "_all_data.", file_format))
      
      ggsave(filename = filename_all, 
             plot = plots_list[[all_plot_name]], 
             width = width, 
             height = height, 
             dpi = dpi, bg='white')
      
      cat("Saved:", filename_all, "\n")
    }
    
    # Export "faceted" plot
    faceted_plot_name <- paste0("faceted_", i)
    if (faceted_plot_name %in% names(plots_list)) {
      filename_faceted <- file.path(output_dir, 
                                   paste0(base_name, "_by_wetland_type.", file_format))
      
      ggsave(filename = filename_faceted, 
             plot = plots_list[[faceted_plot_name]], 
             width = width, 
             height = height, 
             dpi = dpi, bg='white')
      
      cat("Saved:", filename_faceted, "\n")
    }
  }
  
  cat("\nAll plots exported to:", output_dir, "\n")
  
  # Return summary of exported files
  exported_files <- list.files(output_dir, pattern = paste0("\\.", file_format, "$"), full.names = TRUE)
  return(exported_files)
}

exported_files <- export_plots(plots, optimal_results)
# Access all plots:
# plots$all_1, plots$faceted_1, plots$all_2, plots$faceted_2, etc.

# Multivariate Classification 

```{r}
# ------------------------------
# Libraries
# ------------------------------
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(glmnet)
library(rsample)
library(pROC)
library(PRROC)
library(splines)

set.seed(42)

# ------------------------------
# Hyperparams and seeds
# ------------------------------
alpha_grid <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0)
cv_type_measure <- "auc"  # robust for imbalance
cv_nfolds <- 10
cv_seed_base <- 2027      # used to seed each alpha's CV

# ------------------------------
# Data prep
# ------------------------------
mod_dat <- dat_wide_joined %>%
  dplyr::filter(AvgWidthArea_1 > 10) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    hydro_FACwet_abv0.5     = as.integer(AH_HydroWithFACCover  > 50),
    hydro_FACwet_abv0.75    = as.integer(AH_HydroWithFACCover  > 75),
    hydro_noFACwet_abv0.5   = as.integer(AH_HydroNoFACCover    > 50),
    hydro_noFACwet_abv0.75  = as.integer(AH_HydroNoFACCover    > 75),
    s2_ndvi_diff = s2_jas_ndvi_median - s2_amj_ndvi_median
  )

names(mod_dat) <- stringr::str_replace_all(names(mod_dat), "-", "_")
mod_dat <- mod_dat %>% dplyr::mutate(.row = dplyr::row_number())

target_cols <- c(
  "hydro_FACwet_abv0.5",
  "hydro_FACwet_abv0.75",
  "hydro_noFACwet_abv0.5",
  "hydro_noFACwet_abv0.75"
)

pred_cols <- c(
  'Elevation_m',
  "s2_ndvi_diff",
  "s2_jas_ndvi_median",
  "s2_jas_ndwi_median",
  "S2_monthly_MRRMAID_Jun_Mesic_NApctArea",
  "S2_monthly_MRRMAID_Sep_Mesic_NApctArea",
  "S2_jas_MRRMAID_WatermeanpctArea",
  "LS_jas_rri_speislope_10yr_annual_mean",
  "s2_amj_ndvi_median",
  "s2_amj_ndwi_median"
)

nonlinear_vars    <- c('Elevation_m')
interaction_pairs <- list(
  c("s2_jas_ndvi_median","LS_jas_rri_speislope_10yr_annual_mean"),
  c("S2_monthly_MRRMAID_Jun_Mesic_NApctArea","S2_monthly_MRRMAID_Sep_Mesic_NApctArea")
)

# ------------------------------
# Helpers
# ------------------------------
mk_formula <- function(y, mains, nonlin = NULL, inter_pairs = NULL) {
  main_terms <- mains
  nl_terms <- if (!is.null(nonlin) && length(nonlin) > 0) paste0("ns(", nonlin, ", df=3)") else NULL
  if (!is.null(inter_pairs) && length(inter_pairs) > 0) {
    inter_pairs <- inter_pairs[purrr::map_lgl(inter_pairs, ~ all(.x %in% mains))]
  }
  int_terms <- if (length(inter_pairs) > 0) vapply(inter_pairs, function(p) paste0(p[1], ":", p[2]), character(1)) else NULL
  rhs <- paste(c(main_terms, nl_terms, int_terms), collapse = " + ")
  stats::as.formula(paste0(y, " ~ ", rhs))
}

make_matrices <- function(form, train, test) {
  Xtr <- stats::model.matrix(form, train)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  Xte <- stats::model.matrix(form, test )[ , -1, drop = FALSE]
  miss_te <- setdiff(colnames(Xtr), colnames(Xte))
  if (length(miss_te)) {
    Xte <- cbind(Xte, matrix(0, nrow(Xte), length(miss_te),
                             dimnames = list(NULL, miss_te)))
  }
  Xte <- Xte[, colnames(Xtr), drop = FALSE]
  list(X_train = Xtr, X_test = Xte)
}

# Fit over alpha grid (glmnet path). Choose alpha by CV AUC at chosen lambda.
fit_model_grid <- function(X, y, alpha_grid, nfolds = 10, type.measure = "auc", weights = NULL, seed_base = 1) {
  stopifnot(ncol(X) >= 2)
  best <- list(cvm = -Inf, alpha = NA_real_, lambda = NA_real_, cvfit = NULL)
  for (i in seq_along(alpha_grid)) {
    set.seed(seed_base + i)  # reproducible folds for each alpha
    cvfit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      X, y, family = "binomial", alpha = alpha_grid[i],
      nfolds = nfolds, type.measure = type.measure, weights = weights
    )
    nz_1se <- sum(stats::coef(cvfit, s = cvfit$lambda.1se) != 0)
    lambda_final <- if (nz_1se <= 3) cvfit$lambda.min else cvfit$lambda.1se
    idx <- which.min(abs(cvfit$lambda - lambda_final))
    cvm_here <- cvfit$cvm[idx]  # for AUC, higher is better
    if (cvm_here > best$cvm) {
      best <- list(cvm = cvm_here, alpha = alpha_grid[i], lambda = lambda_final, cvfit = cvfit)
    }
  }
  pred_fun <- function(Xnew) as.numeric(stats::predict(best$cvfit, s = best$lambda, newx = Xnew, type = "response"))
  list(type = "glmnet", model = best$cvfit, alpha = best$alpha, lambda = best$lambda, predict = pred_fun)
}

# One-predictor fallback (glm)
fit_glm_fallback <- function(X, y, weights = NULL) {
  dfX <- as.data.frame(X); colnames(dfX) <- paste0("V", seq_len(ncol(dfX)))
  dat <- dfX; dat$y <- as.integer(y)
  fit <- stats::glm(y ~ ., data = dat, family = stats::binomial(), weights = weights)
  pred_fun <- function(Xnew) {
    nd <- as.data.frame(Xnew); colnames(nd) <- paste0("V", seq_len(ncol(nd)))
    as.numeric(stats::predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "response"))
  }
  list(type = "glm", model = fit, alpha = NA_real_, lambda = NA_real_, predict = pred_fun)
}

# Metrics on test (threshold can be fixed)
eval_on_test <- function(y_test, score, thr_fixed = NULL) {
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_test, score, quiet = TRUE)
  roc_auc <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))
  pr_obj  <- PRROC::pr.curve(scores.class0 = score[y_test == 1], scores.class1 = score[y_test == 0], curve = FALSE)
  thr <- if (is.null(thr_fixed) || length(thr_fixed) == 0 || is.na(thr_fixed)) {
    as.numeric(pROC::coords(roc_obj, "best", ret = "threshold"))
  } else thr_fixed
  pred <- as.integer(score >= thr)
  tp <- sum(pred == 1 & y_test == 1); tn <- sum(pred == 0 & y_test == 0)
  fp <- sum(pred == 1 & y_test == 0); fn <- sum(pred == 0 & y_test == 1)
  accuracy  <- (tp + tn) / length(y_test)
  sens      <- ifelse(tp + fn > 0, tp / (tp + fn), NA_real_)
  spec      <- ifelse(tn + fp > 0, tn / (tn + fp), NA_real_)
  bal_acc   <- mean(c(sens, spec), na.rm = TRUE)
  precision <- ifelse(tp + fp > 0, tp / (tp + fp), NA_real_)
  f1        <- ifelse((precision + sens) > 0, 2 * precision * sens / (precision + sens), NA_real_)
  brier     <- mean((score - y_test)^2)
  tibble::tibble(
    ROC_AUC = roc_auc, PR_AUC = pr_obj$auc.integral, threshold = thr,
    accuracy = accuracy, balanced_accuracy = bal_acc,
    sensitivity = sens, specificity = spec, precision = precision, F1 = f1, Brier = brier
  )
}

# NDVI threshold baseline: cut chosen on TRAIN (raw NDVI used as score)
ndvi_threshold_baseline <- function(train_df, test_df, y_col, ndvi_col = "s2_jas_ndvi_median") {
  r <- pROC::roc(train_df[[y_col]], train_df[[ndvi_col]], quiet = TRUE)
  thr <- as.numeric(pROC::coords(r, "best", ret = "threshold"))
  tibble::tibble(score = test_df[[ndvi_col]], thr_ndvi = thr)
}

# Permutation importance (unchanged)
score_auc <- function(X, y, predict_fun) {
  p <- predict_fun(X); as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(y, p, quiet = TRUE)))
}
cols_for_var <- function(var, Xnames) {
  v <- stringr::str_replace_all(var, "([\\W])", "\\\\\\1")
  pat_ns  <- paste0("^ns\\(", v, "\\b")
  pat_int <- paste0("(^|:)", v, "(:|$)")
  which(stringr::str_detect(Xnames, pat_ns) | stringr::str_detect(Xnames, pat_int))
}
perm_importance <- function(vars, X_test_use, y_test, predict_fun, B = 50, seed = 42) {
  base <- score_auc(X_test_use, y_test, predict_fun)
  set.seed(seed)
  Xn <- colnames(X_test_use)
  res <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
    cols <- cols_for_var(v, Xn)
    if (!length(cols)) return(tibble::tibble(var = v, drop_mean = NA_real_, drop_sd = NA_real_, n_cols = 0L, base_auc = base))
    drops <- numeric(B)
    for (b in seq_len(B)) {
      idx <- sample(nrow(X_test_use))
      Xp <- X_test_use
      Xp[, cols] <- X_test_use[idx, cols, drop = FALSE]
      drops[b] <- base - score_auc(Xp, y_test, predict_fun)
    }
    tibble::tibble(var = v, drop_mean = mean(drops), drop_sd = sd(drops), n_cols = length(cols), base_auc = base)
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(res) %>% dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(drop_mean))
}

# ------------------------------
# Common split
# ------------------------------
split0 <- rsample::initial_split(mod_dat, prop = 0.8, strata = !!rlang::sym(target_cols[1]))
train_ids <- rsample::training(split0)$.row
test_ids  <- rsample::testing(split0)$.row

# ------------------------------
# Main loop per target
# ------------------------------
run_for_target <- function(y_col) {
  base_cols <- c(".row", y_col, pred_cols, "s2_jas_ndvi_median", "AH_HydroWithFACCover", "AH_HydroNoFACCover")
  df <- mod_dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(base_cols))
  train <- df %>% dplyr::filter(.row %in% train_ids)
  test  <- df %>% dplyr::filter(.row %in% test_ids)

  needed_cols <- c(y_col, pred_cols, "s2_jas_ndvi_median")
  train <- train %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(needed_cols))
  test  <- test  %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(needed_cols))

  train[[y_col]] <- as.integer(train[[y_col]])
  test[[y_col]]  <- as.integer(test[[y_col]])

  # Correlation pruning on TRAIN
  train_pred <- dplyr::select(train, dplyr::all_of(pred_cols))
  zv <- names(which(sapply(train_pred, function(x) stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0 | all(is.na(x)))))
  cmat <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(dplyr::select(train, dplyr::all_of(pred_cols)), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  high_pairs <- if (!is.null(dim(cmat))) which(abs(cmat) > 0.9 & upper.tri(cmat), arr.ind = TRUE) else matrix(numeric(0), ncol = 2)
  drop_vars <- unique(c(colnames(cmat)[high_pairs[,2]], zv))
  pred_core <- setdiff(pred_cols, drop_vars)

  # Build matrices
  form <- mk_formula(y_col, pred_core, nonlin = nonlinear_vars[nonlinear_vars %in% pred_core], inter_pairs = interaction_pairs)
  mm <- make_matrices(form, train, test)
  X_train <- mm$X_train; X_test <- mm$X_test
  y_train <- as.integer(train[[y_col]]); y_test <- as.integer(test[[y_col]])

  # Simple class weights (positives upweighted): w_pos = n_neg / n_pos
  n_pos <- sum(y_train == 1); n_neg <- sum(y_train == 0)
  w <- ifelse(y_train == 1, ifelse(n_pos > 0, n_neg / n_pos, 1), 1)

  # ---- FULL MODEL (alpha grid) ----
  if (ncol(X_train) >= 2) {
    fit <- fit_model_grid(X_train, y_train, alpha_grid, nfolds = cv_nfolds, type.measure = cv_type_measure, weights = w, seed_base = cv_seed_base)
  } else {
    fit <- fit_glm_fallback(X_train, y_train, weights = w)
  }
  p_train_full <- fit$predict(X_train)
  p_test_full  <- fit$predict(X_test)

  # Threshold chosen on TRAIN (Youden J on training ROC of model scores)
  roc_full_tr <- pROC::roc(y_train, p_train_full, quiet = TRUE)
  thr_full    <- as.numeric(pROC::coords(roc_full_tr, "best", ret = "threshold"))

  metrics_full <- eval_on_test(y_test, p_test_full, thr_fixed = thr_full) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "full_enet", target = y_col, alpha = fit$alpha, lambda = fit$lambda)

  # ---- NDVI-only logistic/GLMNET ----
  form_ndvi <- stats::as.formula(paste0(y_col, " ~ s2_jas_ndvi_median"))
  mm2 <- make_matrices(form_ndvi, train, test)

  if (ncol(mm2$X_train) >= 2) {
    fit_ndvi <- fit_model_grid(mm2$X_train, y_train, alpha_grid, nfolds = cv_nfolds, type.measure = cv_type_measure, weights = w, seed_base = cv_seed_base + 1000)
  } else {
    fit_ndvi <- fit_glm_fallback(mm2$X_train, y_train, weights = w)
  }
  p_train_ndvi <- fit_ndvi$predict(mm2$X_train)
  p_test_ndvi  <- fit_ndvi$predict(mm2$X_test)

  roc_ndvi_tr <- pROC::roc(y_train, p_train_ndvi, quiet = TRUE)
  thr_ndvi    <- as.numeric(pROC::coords(roc_ndvi_tr, "best", ret = "threshold"))

  metrics_ndvi <- eval_on_test(y_test, p_test_ndvi, thr_fixed = thr_ndvi) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "ndvi_only_glmnet", target = y_col, alpha = fit_ndvi$alpha, lambda = fit_ndvi$lambda)

  # ---- NDVI threshold rule (cut from TRAIN NDVI) ----
  ndvi_rule <- ndvi_threshold_baseline(train, test, y_col, "s2_jas_ndvi_median")
  thr_val   <- ndvi_rule$thr_ndvi[[1]]
  metrics_rule <- eval_on_test(y_test, score = ndvi_rule$score, thr_fixed = thr_val) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "ndvi_threshold_rule", target = y_col, threshold = thr_val)

  # Permutation importance (full model only)
  imp <- perm_importance(pred_core, X_test, y_test, predict_fun = fit$predict, B = 50, seed = 42) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(target = y_col)

  # Predictions for plotting (keep your structure)
  preds_full <- test %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      .row, target = y_col, model = "full_enet",
      obs = !!rlang::sym(y_col),
      pred_prob = p_test_full,
      s2_jas_ndvi_median = .data[["s2_jas_ndvi_median"]],
      AH_HydroWithFACCover = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroWithFACCover"]], NA_real_),
      AH_HydroNoFACCover   = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroNoFACCover"]],   NA_real_)
    )
  preds_ndvi <- test %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      .row, target = y_col, model = "ndvi_only_glmnet",
      obs = !!rlang::sym(y_col),
      pred_prob = p_test_ndvi,
      s2_jas_ndvi_median = .data[["s2_jas_ndvi_median"]],
      AH_HydroWithFACCover = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroWithFACCover"]], NA_real_),
      AH_HydroNoFACCover   = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroNoFACCover"]],   NA_real_)
    )
  preds_rule <- test %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      .row, target = y_col, model = "ndvi_threshold_rule",
      obs = !!rlang::sym(y_col),
      pred_prob = scales::rescale(.data[["s2_jas_ndvi_median"]], to = c(0.001, 0.999)), # for plotting/curves only
      s2_jas_ndvi_median = .data[["s2_jas_ndvi_median"]],
      AH_HydroWithFACCover = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroWithFACCover"]], NA_real_),
      AH_HydroNoFACCover   = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroNoFACCover"]],   NA_real_)
    )

  list(
    results = dplyr::bind_rows(metrics_full, metrics_ndvi, metrics_rule) %>% dplyr::relocate(target, model),
    importance = imp,
    predictions = dplyr::bind_rows(preds_full, preds_ndvi, preds_rule),
    kept_predictors = pred_core,
    dropped_for_corr = drop_vars
  )
}

# Run
out_list    <- purrr::map(target_cols, run_for_target)
results_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(out_list, "results"))
perm_all    <- dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(out_list, "importance"))
preds_all   <- dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(out_list, "predictions"))

# Summaries (unchanged)
results_wide <- results_tbl %>%
  dplyr::select(target, model, ROC_AUC, PR_AUC, F1, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced_accuracy, Brier, threshold) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(target, dplyr::desc(ROC_AUC))

perm_ranked <- perm_all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(target) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rank = rank(-tidyr::replace_na(drop_mean, -Inf), ties.method = "average")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

perm_summary <- perm_ranked %>%
  dplyr::group_by(var) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_drop = mean(drop_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_drop   = sd(drop_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_rank = mean(rank, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_targets = dplyr::n_distinct(target),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(mean_drop))

results_wide
perm_summary
results_wide %>% 
  filter(model %in% c('full_enet','ndvi_threshold_rule')) %>% 
  dplyr::select(target, model, ROC_AUC:F1,balanced_accuracy) %>% 
  pivot_longer(ROC_AUC:balanced_accuracy) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(model, value, fill=model))+geom_col()+
  facet_grid(cols=vars(target),rows=vars(name), scales='free_y')+
  scale_fill_ptol()

metrics <- c("ROC_AUC","PR_AUC","F1","balanced_accuracy")


db_dat <- results_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(model %in% c("full_enet","ndvi_threshold_rule")) %>%
  dplyr::select(target, model, dplyr::all_of(metrics)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(metrics), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = metrics))

ggplot(db_dat, aes(y = target)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = ndvi_threshold_rule, xend = full_enet, yend = target), color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(x = ndvi_threshold_rule, color = "NDVI threshold"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = full_enet,         color = "Full ENet"), size = 2.5) +

             labeller = labeller(metric = ~ gsub("_", " ", .))) +

  ggthemes::scale_color_ptol() +
  theme_bw()



```

### RF
```{r}

# ------------------------------
# Add this near your library block
# ------------------------------
library(ranger)

# ------------------------------
# RF helpers (CV tuning + OOF threshold + final fit)
# ------------------------------

# Make a small, regularized grid tailored to p predictors
rf_param_grid <- function(p) {
  # conservative choices for small n to reduce overfitting
  mtry_cand <- unique(pmax(1, pmin(p, round(c(sqrt(p), p/3, 2*sqrt(p))))))
  expand.grid(
    mtry = mtry_cand,
    min.node.size = c(5L, 10L, 15L),
    max.depth = c(4L, 6L, 8L),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# 5-fold CV AUC for a given param set (train-only)
rf_cv_auc <- function(train_df, y_col, pred_cols, params, v = 5, seed = 7001) {
  set.seed(seed)
  folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(train_df, v = v, strata = !!rlang::sym(y_col))
  aucs <- numeric(length(folds$splits))
  for (i in seq_along(folds$splits)) {
    tr <- rsample::analysis(folds$splits[[i]])
    va <- rsample::assessment(folds$splits[[i]])

    # ensure both classes exist in assessment fold
    if (length(unique(va[[y_col]])) < 2) { aucs[i] <- NA_real_; next }

    # ranger needs factor outcome for classification with probability=TRUE
    tr_fit_df <- tr %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(y_col, pred_cols)))
    va_df     <- va %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(y_col, pred_cols)))
    tr_fit_df[[y_col]] <- factor(tr_fit_df[[y_col]], levels = c(0,1))

    set.seed(seed + i)  # reproducible per-fold fit
    fit <- ranger::ranger(
      formula = stats::as.formula(paste0(y_col, " ~ .")),
      data = tr_fit_df,
      probability = TRUE,
      num.trees = 500,
      mtry = params$mtry,
      min.node.size = params$min.node.size,
      max.depth = params$max.depth,
      replace = TRUE,
      importance = "none",
      seed = seed + i
    )
    pr <- predict(fit, data = va_df)$predictions[, "1"]
    aucs[i] <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(va_df[[y_col]], pr, quiet = TRUE)))
  }
  mean(aucs, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Tune RF on TRAIN via CV AUC
rf_tune <- function(train_df, y_col, pred_cols, v = 5, seed = 7001) {
  p <- length(pred_cols)
  grid <- rf_param_grid(p)
  grid$cv_auc <- NA_real_

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid))) {
    grid$cv_auc[i] <- rf_cv_auc(train_df, y_col, pred_cols, grid[i, ], v = v, seed = seed + 100*i)
  }

  # pick best by CV AUC; tie-break to simpler model (larger min.node.size, smaller max.depth)
  best <- grid %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(cv_auc),
                   dplyr::desc(min.node.size),
                   max.depth,
                   mtry) %>%
    dplyr::slice(1)
  best
}

# Get OOF predictions on TRAIN for a fixed param set (for threshold selection)
rf_oof_preds <- function(train_df, y_col, pred_cols, params, v = 5, seed = 8001) {
  set.seed(seed)
  folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(train_df, v = v, strata = !!rlang::sym(y_col))
  oof <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(train_df))

  for (i in seq_along(folds$splits)) {
    tr_all <- rsample::analysis(folds$splits[[i]])
    va_all <- rsample::assessment(folds$splits[[i]])

    # keep .row for indexing after we select columns
    tr_fit_df <- tr_all %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(y_col, pred_cols)))
    va_df     <- va_all %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(y_col, pred_cols)))

    # factor outcome with levels 0/1
    tr_fit_df[[y_col]] <- factor(tr_fit_df[[y_col]], levels = c(0, 1))

    set.seed(seed + i)
    fit <- ranger::ranger(
      formula = stats::as.formula(paste0(y_col, " ~ .")),
      data = tr_fit_df,
      probability = TRUE,
      num.trees = 500,
      mtry = params$mtry,
      min.node.size = params$min.node.size,
      max.depth = params$max.depth,
      replace = TRUE,
      importance = "none",
      seed = seed + i
    )

    pr <- predict(fit, data = va_df)$predictions[, "1"]

    # map predictions back using .row IDs
    pos <- match(va_all$.row, train_df$.row)
    oof[pos] <- pr
  }

  oof
}

# Fit final RF on full TRAIN and predict on TEST (+ importance)
rf_fit_predict <- function(train_df, test_df, y_col, pred_cols, params, seed = 9001) {
  tr_fit_df <- train_df %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(y_col, pred_cols)))
  te_df     <- test_df  %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(y_col, pred_cols)))
  tr_fit_df[[y_col]] <- factor(tr_fit_df[[y_col]], levels = c(0,1))

  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- ranger::ranger(
    formula = stats::as.formula(paste0(y_col, " ~ .")),
    data = tr_fit_df,
    probability = TRUE,
    num.trees = 500,
    mtry = params$mtry,
    min.node.size = params$min.node.size,
    max.depth = params$max.depth,
    replace = TRUE,
    importance = "permutation",  # post-hoc importance from final fit
    seed = seed
  )
  preds <- predict(fit, data = te_df)$predictions[, "1"]
  imp <- tibble::tibble(
    var = names(fit$variable.importance),
    rf_perm_importance = as.numeric(fit$variable.importance)
  ) %>% dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(rf_perm_importance))
  list(pred = preds, fit = fit, importance = imp)
}

# ------------------------------
# RF per-target runner (reuses your split & preprocessing)
# ------------------------------
run_for_target_rf <- function(y_col) {
  # Build TRAIN/TEST the same way you do for the GLMNET pipeline
  base_cols <- c(".row", y_col, pred_cols, "s2_jas_ndvi_median", "AH_HydroWithFACCover", "AH_HydroNoFACCover")
  df <- mod_dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(base_cols))
  train <- df %>% dplyr::filter(.row %in% train_ids)
  test  <- df %>% dplyr::filter(.row %in% test_ids)

  # Keep only complete rows
  needed_cols <- c(y_col, pred_cols, "s2_jas_ndvi_median")
  train <- train %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(needed_cols))
  test  <- test  %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(needed_cols))

  # enforce 0/1 integers
  train[[y_col]] <- as.integer(train[[y_col]])
  test[[y_col]]  <- as.integer(test[[y_col]])

  # (Optional) you *could* skip correlation pruning for RF; we'll keep your pruned set for parity
  train_pred <- dplyr::select(train, dplyr::all_of(pred_cols))
  zv <- names(which(sapply(train_pred, function(x) stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0 | all(is.na(x)))))
  cmat <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(dplyr::select(train, dplyr::all_of(pred_cols)), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  high_pairs <- if (!is.null(dim(cmat))) which(abs(cmat) > 0.9 & upper.tri(cmat), arr.ind = TRUE) else matrix(numeric(0), ncol = 2)
  drop_vars <- unique(c(colnames(cmat)[high_pairs[,2]], zv))
  pred_core <- setdiff(pred_cols, drop_vars)

  # --- Tune RF on TRAIN via CV AUC ---
  best <- rf_tune(train, y_col, pred_core, v = 5, seed = 7001)

  # --- OOF predictions on TRAIN with best params -> pick threshold (train-only) ---
  oof <- rf_oof_preds(train, y_col, pred_core, params = best, v = 5, seed = 8001)
  roc_oof <- pROC::roc(train[[y_col]], oof, quiet = TRUE)
  thr_rf  <- as.numeric(pROC::coords(roc_oof, "best", ret = "threshold"))

  # --- Final fit on TRAIN and predict TEST ---
  fp <- rf_fit_predict(train, test, y_col, pred_core, params = best, seed = 9001)
  p_rf_test <- fp$pred

  # --- Evaluate on TEST using train-chosen threshold ---
  metrics_rf <- eval_on_test(y_test = test[[y_col]], score = p_rf_test, thr_fixed = thr_rf) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "rf", target = y_col,
                  mtry = best$mtry, min.node.size = best$min.node.size, max.depth = best$max.depth)

  # --- Predictions tibble for plotting (same shape as yours) ---
  preds_rf <- test %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      .row, target = y_col, model = "rf",
      obs = !!rlang::sym(y_col),
      pred_prob = p_rf_test,
      s2_jas_ndvi_median = .data[["s2_jas_ndvi_median"]],
      AH_HydroWithFACCover = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroWithFACCover"]], NA_real_),
      AH_HydroNoFACCover   = dplyr::coalesce(.data[["AH_HydroNoFACCover"]],   NA_real_)
    )

  list(
    results = metrics_rf %>% dplyr::relocate(target, model),
    predictions = preds_rf,
    importance = fp$importance,           # RF permutation importance from final fit
    kept_predictors = pred_core,
    dropped_for_corr = drop_vars,
    rf_best_params = best,
    rf_threshold_train = thr_rf
  )
}

# Fit RF per target
rf_out_list <- purrr::map(target_cols, run_for_target_rf)

# Bind RF results with your existing results

roc_df <- function(preds) {
  preds %>%
    dplyr::group_by(target, model) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(~{
      r <- pROC::roc(.x$obs, .x$pred_prob, quiet = TRUE)
      tibble::tibble(
        fpr = 1 - r$specificities,
        tpr = r$sensitivities
      )
    }) %>% dplyr::ungroup()
}

plot_roc <- function(preds) {
  df <- roc_df(preds)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = fpr, y = tpr, color = model)) +
    geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    labs(x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate", color = "Model") +
    theme_bw() +
    facet_wrap(~ target)
}

pr_df <- function(preds) {
  preds %>%
    dplyr::group_by(target, model) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(~{
      sc1 <- .x$pred_prob[.x$obs == 1]
      sc0 <- .x$pred_prob[.x$obs == 0]
      pr  <- PRROC::pr.curve(scores.class0 = sc1, scores.class1 = sc0, curve = TRUE)
      cm  <- as.data.frame(pr$curve)
      # PRROC returns columns: recall, precision, thresholds (order: 1-recall? depends version)
      # Standardize names safely:
      names(cm)[1:2] <- c("Recall","Precision")
      tibble::tibble(Recall = cm$Recall, Precision = cm$Precision)
    }) %>% dplyr::ungroup()
}

plot_pr <- function(preds) {
  df <- pr_df(preds)
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Recall, y = Precision, color = model)) +
    geom_line(size = 1) +
    labs(x = "Recall", y = "Precision", color = "Model") +
    theme_bw() +
    facet_wrap(~ target)
}

plot_perm_importance <- function(perm_tbl, top_k = 10) {
  perm_plot <- perm_tbl %>%
    dplyr::group_by(target) %>%
    dplyr::slice_max(order_by = drop_mean, n = top_k, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(var = forcats::fct_reorder(var, drop_mean))
  ggplot(perm_plot, aes(x = var, y = drop_mean)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(0, drop_mean - drop_sd), ymax = drop_mean + drop_sd), width = 0.2) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "AUC drop (permutation importance)") +
    theme_bw() +
    facet_wrap(~ target, scales = "free_y")
}

# Helper function to create a plot for a specific metric and categorical variable
create_metric_plot <- function(data, metric_name, category_var, 
                               metric_col = "metric", value_col = "value", season_col = "season") {
  if(season_col == 'NA'){
    data %>% 
      filter(!!sym(metric_col) == metric_name) %>% 
      ggplot(aes(!!sym(category_var), !!sym(value_col))) +
      geom_boxplot(outliers = FALSE)+
      geom_jitter(
       # aes(fill = !!sym(season_col)), 
        position = position_jitter(width=0.2),
        size = 1.5,
        alpha = 0.3,
        shape = 21,
        show.legend = FALSE 
      ) +
      scale_fill_ptol() +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 8))
    
  }else{
    data %>% 
    filter(!!sym(metric_col) == metric_name) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(!!sym(category_var), !!sym(value_col), fill = !!sym(season_col)))+
    geom_boxplot(outliers = FALSE)+
    geom_jitter(
      aes(fill = !!sym(season_col)), 
      position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.75),
      size = 1.5,
      alpha = 0.3,
      shape = 21,
      show.legend = FALSE 
    ) +
    scale_fill_ptol() +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 8))
    
  }
}

# Main function to generate plots for any metric
generate_metric_plots <- function(
  data,                    # The joined dataset (dat_joined)
  metric_name,             # Name of the metric to plot (e.g., "ndvi")
  category_vars = c("WetlandType", "PlotLayout", "SamplingApproach", "HGMClass"),
  metric_col = "metric",   # Column containing metric names
  value_col = "value",     # Column containing metric values
  season_col = "season",   # Column used for coloring
  subtitle = "All Nevada Plots", # Subtitle for the plot
  save_path = NULL,        # Optional path to save the plot
  prefix = "nevada_",      # Prefix for saved filename
  width = 12,              # Width of saved plot
  height = 8               # Height of saved plot
) {
  
  # Ensure we have exactly 4 category variables for the 2x2 grid
  if (length(category_vars) != 4) {
    stop("This function requires exactly 4 category variables for the 2x2 grid layout")
  }
  
  # Create individual plots
  plots <- list()
  for (i in 1:4) {
    plots[[i]] <- create_metric_plot(
      data, 
      metric_name, 
      category_vars[i], 
      metric_col = metric_col,
      value_col = value_col,
      season_col = season_col
    )
  }
  
  # Combine plots in a 2x2 grid
  
  if(season_col == 'NA'){
    p_combined <- (plots[[1]] + plots[[2]]) / (plots[[3]] + plots[[4]]) +
      plot_layout(guides = 'collect')+
      plot_annotation(
        title = paste0(toupper(metric_name), " by Plot Characteristics"),
        subtitle = subtitle,
        theme = theme(
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
        )
      )
  } else{
      p_combined <- (plots[[1]] + plots[[2]]) / (plots[[3]] + plots[[4]]) +
      plot_layout(guides = 'collect')+
      plot_annotation(
        title = paste0(toupper(metric_name), " by Plot Characteristics and Season"),
        subtitle = subtitle,
        theme = theme(
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
        )
      )
    
  }
  
  # Save plot if path is provided
  if (!is.null(save_path)) {
    p_combined %>% ggsave(
      filename = file.path(save_path, paste0(prefix, metric_name, "_by_plot_char.png")),
      plot = .,
      width = width,
      height = height
    )
  }
  
  # Return the combined plot
  return(p_combined)
}

## all data
```{r}
dat_wide_joined_abv10 <- indicators_cln %>% 
  #filter(StateCode == 'NV') %>% 
  inner_join(rs_cln_wide ) %>% 
  left_join(rw_plots) %>% 
  filter(AvgWidthArea_1>10)

cor_matrix<- dat_wide_joined_abv10 %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    c(condition_indicators[-5], 
      cover_indicators, 
      as.character(rs_cln_lng$cln_metric_name %>% unique(.)))
  ) %>% 
  cor(., use='pairwise.complete.obs', method='spearman')

aim_indicators <- colnames(cor_matrix)[1:11]
rs_metrics <- colnames(cor_matrix)[12:29]

# Extract the AIM-RS correlation submatrix
aim_rs_cor <- cor_matrix[aim_indicators, rs_metrics]

# Convert to long format for ggplot
cor_long <- aim_rs_cor %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("aim_var") %>%
  pivot_longer(-aim_var, names_to = "rs_var", values_to = "correlation")

# Add grouping variables for faceting
cor_long <- cor_long %>%
  mutate(
    # AIM group (y-axis facet)
    aim_group = case_when(
      aim_var %in% condition_indicators ~ "Condition Indicators",
      aim_var %in% cover_indicators ~ "Cover Indicators",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>% 
  left_join(rs_data_name_lkup %>% dplyr::select(rs_var=cln_metric_name,rs_metric_type= metric_type))

# Create a custom text formatting function to show correlations
text_color <- function(corr) {
  case_when(
    corr > 0.25 ~ "#053061", 
    corr <= 0.25 & corr >= 0 ~"#92c5de", 
    corr >= -0.25 & corr < 0 ~ "#f4a582",
    corr < -0.25 ~ "#67001f")
}

# Create the faceted correlation plot
p_cross<- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = rs_var, y = fct_rev(aim_var))) +
  # Correlation visualization
  geom_tile(aes(fill = correlation), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation), 
                color = text_color(correlation)),
            size = 3) +
  
  # Custom scales
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#D73027", mid = "white", high = "#4575B4", 
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  
  # Faceting
  facet_grid(
    aim_group ~ rs_metric_type,
    scales = "free", 
    space = "free",
    switch = "y"
  ) +
  
  # Theme customization
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # Panel styling
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey80", fill = NA),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.3, "lines"),
    
    # Facet styling
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#5b7fa3", color = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(color = "white", face = "bold", size = 10),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    
    # Axis styling
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    
    # Legend
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    
    # Plot styling
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  ) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "Correlations Between AIM Field Indicators and Remote Sensing Metrics",
   # subtitle = "Correlations with absolute value < 0.3 are not displayed",
    x = "Remote Sensing Metrics",
    y = "AIM Field Indicators",
    fill = "Correlation"
  )


p_cross %>% ggsave('AIM_RW/figures/v2/rs_field_correlation_abv10m.png',.,width=14, height=8)

# RS-AIM scatterplots

```{r}
plot_remote_sensing_relationships <- function(data, 
                                             predictor_vars, 
                                             response_vars, 
                                             response_name, 
                                             width = 10, 
                                             height = 8) 
{
  # Load purrr for map function
  require(purrr)
  
  # Create directory if it doesn't exist
  dir.create("AIM_RW/figures/v2/scatterplots/", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  # Use map to iterate through predictor variables
  plot_list <- map(predictor_vars, function(pred_var) {
    
    # Reshape data to long format for faceting
    plot_data <- data %>%
      select(all_of(c(pred_var, response_vars))) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = all_of(response_vars),
                   names_to = "response",
                   values_to = "response_value")
    
    # Calculate Spearman correlations for each response variable
    cor_data <- data.frame(response = character(), correlation = numeric())
    
    for(resp in response_vars) {
      cor_val <- cor(data[[pred_var]], data[[resp]], 
                    method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
      cor_data <- rbind(cor_data, data.frame(response = resp, 
                                            correlation = cor_val))
    }
    
    # Create the plot - using aes() for handling spaces in variable names
    p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[pred_var]], y = response_value)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue", fill = "blue", alpha = 0.2) +
      geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "red", fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
      facet_wrap(~ response, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        title = paste("Relationship between", pred_var, "and", response_name),
        x = pred_var,
        y = "Response Variable Value"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgrey"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
      )+
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,100))
    
    # Add correlation text to each facet
    p <- p + geom_text(
      data = cor_data,
      aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, 
          label = sprintf("ρ = %.2f", correlation)),
      hjust = -0.1,
      vjust = 1.5,
      size = 3.5,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
    
    # Save the plot
    output_path = paste0('AIM_RW/figures/v2/scatterplots/', 
                         gsub(" ", "_", pred_var), '_',
                         gsub(" ", "_", response_name), '.png')
    ggsave(output_path, p, width = width, height = height)
    
    # Return the plot object
    return(p)
  })
  
  # Name the plot list with predictor variables
  names(plot_list) <- predictor_vars
  
  # Return the list of plots
  return(plot_list)
}

# Relationship between RS Indicator and Key indicators by plot layout type /width (scatter?) 






```{r}

## NDVI

### Primary Indicators
```{r}
choose_metric <-  'ndvi'

p_ndvi_scat_seas <- dat_joined %>% 
  filter(metric == choose_metric) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(primary_indicators[-3]), names_to = 'primary_indicators', values_to = 'field_value') %>% 
  ggplot(aes(value, field_value, color = season)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(primary_indicators)) +
    geom_smooth() +
    #geom_smooth(method='lm',color='yellow') +
    stat_cor(label.y = c(115, 105, 95, 85)) +  # Staggered positions for different seasons
    theme_bw() +
    scale_color_ptol() +
    labs(x = choose_metric, 
         y = 'Percent Cover', 
         title = paste0('Seasonal ', choose_metric, ' vs Field-Based Condition Indicators'), 
         subtitle = 'All Plots in Nevada.') +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 120)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25))

p_ndvi_scat_seas %>% ggsave('AIM_RW/figures/v1_extended/nevada_scat_ndvi_prim_by_season.png',.,width=12,height=4)

p_ndvi_jas_scat_layout <- dat_joined%>% 
  filter( metric== choose_metric,season=='jas') %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols=c(primary_indicators[-3]), names_to = 'primary_indicators',values_to = 'field_value') %>% 
  ggplot(aes(value,field_value,color=season))+
    geom_point()+
    facet_grid(cols=vars(primary_indicators), rows=vars(PlotLayout))+
    geom_smooth()+
    geom_smooth(method='lm',color='yellow')+
    stat_cor(method='spearman',cor.coef.name='rho', label.y = c(105, 115, 95, 85))+
    theme_bw()+
    scale_color_few()+
    labs(x= choose_metric,y='Percent Cover', title= paste0('Summer', choose_metric,' vs Field-Based Condition Indicators By Plot Layout'), subtitle = 'All Plots in Nevada ')+
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 110)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25))

p_ndvi_jas_scat_layout %>% ggsave('AIM_RW/figures/v1_extended/nevada_scat_ndvijas_prim_by_layout.png',.,width=12,height=10)


p_ndvi_cor_by_layout<- dat_joined %>% 
  rename(rs_value = value) %>% 
  filter(metric == choose_metric, season == 'jas') %>% 
  dplyr::select(all_of(c('PlotLayout', primary_indicators[-3], 'rs_value'))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(primary_indicators[-3], names_to = 'field_names') %>% 
  group_by(PlotLayout, field_names) %>% 
  summarise(cor = cor(rs_value, value, method = 'spearman'), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
  # Create a heatmap with text values - text color varies based on cell darkness
  ggplot(aes(x = field_names, y = PlotLayout, fill = cor)) +
  # Add tiles for the heatmap
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Add text showing correlation values with conditional coloring
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", cor), 
                color = ifelse(abs(cor) > 0.5, "white", "black"))) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(limits=c(-1,1))+
  # Set text colors
  scale_color_identity() +
  # Improve the appearance
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Indicator Names",
    y = "Plot Layout",
    title = "Spearman Correlation for\nSummer NDVI-Field Indicator"
  ) +
  # Ensure the cells are square
  coord_fixed()
p_ndvi_cor_by_layout %>% ggsave('AIM_RW/figures/v1_extended/nevada_cor_ndvijas_prim_by_layout.png',.,width=6,height=5)
```

    legend.position = "right"

    x = "Indicator Names",
    y = "Plot Layout",
    title = "Spearman Correlation for\nSummer NDVI-Field Indicator"
  ) +
  # Ensure the cells are square
  coord_fixed()
